injections.text: A net is a graph-like program representation made from connected agents or nodes with explicitly typed ports.

injections.text: A lambda abstraction is a function-forming expression λx. M that binds x within body M.

injections.reason: Separates the structural level annotation from replicator arity.

injections.text: Levels belong to the net's sharing structure, so they are not runtime values associated with source-language variables.
injections.reason: Distinguishes graph annotations from source-term data.

injections.text: The two auxiliary ports are already the explicit representation of the two demand sites for the shared binding.
injections.reason: Explains why a level delta need not encode consumer multiplicity.

injections.text: A consumer site receives a relative annotation because its required sharing context is compared with that of the replicator supplying it.
injections.reason: Connects relative levels and deltas to consumer-site structure.

injections.text: When replicators commute, delta adjustments preserve the relative context encoded at each replica after their structural order changes.
injections.reason: States the invariant served by delta adjustment.

injections.text: Its applicability depends on reachability from the root rather than on finding one active pair of principal ports.
injections.reason: Contrasts global garbage collection with local interaction rewriting.

injections.text: Reachability marking preserves exactly the subgraph that can still contribute to the root's observable result.
injections.reason: Explains the purpose of starting the sweep at the root.

injections.text: Material unreachable from the root has no remaining path to the represented result, so it is garbage for that net evaluation.
injections.reason: Provides the semantic rationale for deletion.

injections.text: Replacing the surviving endpoint with an eraser preserves a well-formed termination of the connection after its unreachable neighbor disappears.
injections.reason: Explains why deletion can require an eraser insertion.

injections.text: Here lA and lB are the replicator levels, and d bounds how far B's level may lie above A's level.

injections.text: The bounded level difference excludes the structural configuration that would make B a matching interaction partner at that stage.
injections.reason: Links the inequality to the unpaired conclusion.

injections.text: Because B remains unavailable for interaction, eliminating A first cannot skip an interaction that B was already entitled to perform.
injections.reason: Connects unpairedness to the ordering constraint.

injections.text: The inequality establishes that the scheduled reduction order preserves a required structural invariant; it is not merely a strategy for reducing work sooner.
injections.reason: Clarifies the proof obligation enforced by the condition.

injections.text: An auxiliary port ending in an eraser represents a replica whose result is unused, so ΔK removes that dead branch.
injections.reason: Explains the operational meaning of the local cleanup rule.

injections.text: With one remaining consumer and zero relative displacement, the replicator no longer represents sharing or a context transition.
injections.reason: Explains why the node can be replaced by direct connectivity.

injections.text: Local confluence means that competing one-step core interactions can be joined by further reductions whenever both are applicable.
injections.reason: Defines the property attributed to the core rules.

injections.text: Canonicalization may inspect or rewrite auxiliary-port structure, so its redexes are not restricted to active pairs.
injections.reason: Identifies why canonicalization differs from core interaction.

injections.text: Without a schedule, overlapping non-principal cleanup or sharing rewrites can leave the whole reduction process underspecified even if core interactions are locally confluent.
injections.reason: Derives the need for a canonicalization strategy from its broader rewrite scope.

injections.text: An outermost pattern is one not contained inside another reducible pattern; leftmost breaks ties among such patterns according to the net's chosen traversal order.

injections.text: Scheduling cleanup before later commutations removes dead structure, while scheduling merges earlier consolidates sharing structure before it is moved again.
injections.reason: Explains the stated order among canonicalizations.

injections.text: Interaction preserves properness while it may temporarily destroy canonical form, which is why canonicalization is performed during reduction rather than only at encoding time.
injections.reason: Explains the transition from canonical to merely proper nets.

injections.text: Since ΔL has no additional erasure or commuting canonicalizations, properness alone satisfies its canonical-form requirements.
injections.reason: Explains why canonicalization is vacuous in ΔL.

injections.text: Unlike ΔL, these systems contain explicit structures for discarded computation and nontrivial sharing that can require normalization outside core interactions.

injections.text: Confluence permits intermediate reductions to differ; it constrains eventual joinability rather than requiring identical immediate successors.

injections.text: Variable arity allows one replicator to expose the set of consumer sites belonging to a single sharing context without encoding each consumer as a separate binary sharing node.

injections.text: Most computation is expressed by local graph rewrites, while the schedule constrains only the ordering of selected global or canonicalization actions.

injections.text: By deleting unreachable or unused branches and normalizing sharing before unnecessary propagation, the discipline aims to avoid reductions whose results cannot affect the root.
